newsitem.title: GERMANY: German right-winger on trial for killing policeman.
newsitem.headline: German right-winger on trial for killing policeman.

text.p: A German far-right extremist who believes the state is his mortal enemy went on trial on Friday accused of murdering one policeman and attempting to kill others in a shoot-out.

Twenty-five-year-old Kay Diesner admitted to a court in the northern city of Luebeck that he had shot and killed a policeman who attempted to carry out a routine traffic inspection on the Hamburg-Berlin motorway in February.

But Diesner denied murder, claiming a "right of defence against the state". Diesner, a member of the far-right White Aryan Resistance movement, said the state had declared war on him and that police had in the past persecuted him.
"Everything in me just exploded," Diesner told the court, describing his reaction to being stopped for inspection.
Diesner was finally captured after a car chase and a shoot-out. Police later discovered that his car was loaded with munitions.

Diesner is also charged with shooting and wounding a Berlin bookdealer whose business is in a building used by the communist Party of Democratic Socialism, a few days before the attack on the policeman.
